articles.title: How Boris Becker’s financial and legal troubles transformed his public image beyond his celebrated tennis career, from Wimbledon glory to bankruptcy, conviction and prison time
articles.summary: Explore the dramatic transformation of Boris Becker from tennis legend to bankruptcy and legal troubles, detailing his achievements, financial struggles, and legal convictions that altered his public image.
articles.body: Boris Becker was once the very definition of tennis excellence, and the German was the youngest male to win the Wimbledon singles title in 1985, at just 17, beginning a career that would ultimately yield him six Grand Slam singles championships and worldwide fame. His success made him one of Germany’s most celebrated sporting figures.However, the years following his retirement in 1999 brought a very different set of headlines. Financial difficulties, personal controversies, a bankruptcy declaration in the United Kingdom and a prison sentence gradually overshadowed parts of his sporting legacy. Becker's story was an illustration of how a remarkable playing career does not necessarily translate into financial security or shield a public reputation from legal woes.Details on Boris Becker’s fall from Wimbledon champion to prisonSince the end of his playing career, Becker’s public image has changed dramatically. His achievements continued to be respected throughout the tennis world, but the focus increasingly shifted to his personal relationships, financial choices and legal disputes. His later work as a commentator and coach provided a way back into the sport, but the bankruptcy proceedings and the criminal case brought renewed scrutiny.Becker announced himself to the world at Wimbledon in 1985, defeating Kevin Curren in the final to win the championship aged 17. He became the first unseeded player to win the men's singles title at the tournament and quickly developed into an international sporting sensation.His success continued beyond that breakthrough. Becker won three Wimbledon titles, two Australian Open championships and one US Open singles title. He also became the world No. 1, winning 49 singles titles in his professional career.After his retirement in 1999, Becker stayed involved in the sport through TV commentary and coaching. He has been particularly successful with Novak Djokovic during the 2014-16 period, when the Serb won six Grand Slam titles. Becker also became a familiar face and voice on tennis broadcasting, including for the BBC. These roles helped maintain his sporting relevance even as his private life attracted media attention.Why Boris Becker’s financial troubles led to bankruptcyBecker’s financial difficulties became a major public issue after his retirement. During his 2022 trial, he told the court that his career earnings of approximately $50 million had been reduced by divorce costs, child maintenance payments and expensive lifestyle commitments. He also said he took a sharp drop in income after leaving professional tennis.His debts included property-related borrowing and other obligations. The financial strain that led to bankruptcy reportedly came from a loan from private bank Arbuthnot Latham and more borrowing, according to testimony during the trial. His defense also pointed to his reliance on financial advisers and difficulties managing his money.What led to Boris Becker’s 2017 bankruptcy?On June 21, 2017, Becker was declared bankrupt by a London court after failing to repay a substantial loan connected to his property in Mallorca, Spain. His finances were examined in the bankruptcy proceedings and he had to disclose assets and financial transactions to the appointed trustees.The case also included items related to his tennis career. His collection was auctioned in 2019 to raise money for creditors. The auction included significant sporting items, reflecting how his financial situation had reached beyond ordinary personal expenses and into his professional legacy.The scale of his liabilities became another subject of public discussion. Reports during the proceedings described debts approaching £50 million. Becker disputed some claims about his financial position, but the bankruptcy case continued and eventually led to criminal proceedings over the disclosure of assets and transactions.How Boris Becker’s legal convictions changed his legacyBecker’s legal difficulties predated his 2017 bankruptcy. In 2002, he was convicted in Germany of tax evasion and attempted tax evasion, receiving a two-year suspended prison sentence and a financial penalty. The case became an early indication of the challenges that would later affect his public image.The most serious consequences followed the UK bankruptcy proceedings. Becker was convicted by a jury at Southwark Crown Court in April 2022 of four counts under the Insolvency Act. The charges included concealing debt, removing property and failing to disclose assets and financial information required during the bankruptcy process.The trial also heard of claims of precious items, including trophies from Wimbledon. But Becker was acquitted of several charges, including claims that he failed to hand over his trophies and medals. It is important to separate those allegations from the four offenses he was in fact convicted of.Becker was convicted on April 29, 2022, and sentenced to two years and six months in prison. The court's decision marked a dramatic change in the public story of a player who had once been celebrated for his achievements at the All England Club.How prison and deportation affected Boris Becker’s reputationBecker served eight months of his sentence before being released in December 2022 under an early-release arrangement for foreign nationals. He was subsequently deported from the United Kingdom to Germany. The experience brought another major change to his professional life, particularly because he had spent years working in British tennis broadcasting and living in London.2024 was also a critical year in his bankruptcy process. He was discharged from bankruptcy by a UK court after agreeing a settlement with the trustees. The decision came after the finalizing of arrangements for a significant payment and the outstanding obligations in his case.His comments showed how the consequences of the case continued to affect his relationship with the country and the tournament that had defined his sporting career.What Boris Becker’s public image looks like beyond tennisBecker’s legacy now carries two contrasting chapters. His achievements as a six-time Grand Slam singles champion remain an important part of tennis history, while his bankruptcy and insolvency convictions have become equally prominent in accounts of his life after retirement.His role as commentator and coach showed he could be a force in tennis beyond his playing days. But the legal proceedings altered the nature of the telling of his story after his career, making it less about sporting success and more about fiscal responsibility and personal accountability.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Alcaraz sobrevive a un apagón y sigue luchando por París
articles.standfirst: Tuvo bolas de partido en contra pero ganó a Fritz en tres sets para pasar a semifinales
articles.summary: Tuvo bolas de partido en contra pero ganó a Fritz en tres sets para pasar a semifinales
articles.body: Parecía que Taylor Fritz iba a hacer en los cuartos de final del Masters 1.000 de París lo que tenía que hacer y Carlos Alcaraz no iba a ser capaz de hacerlo. Pero al final se llegó al resultado teóricamente lógico por un camino tortuoso que generó un partido apasionante, quizá no el mejor que pueden jugar Alcaraz y Fritz, pero sí sumamente apasionante y competido. Y al final lo ganó Alcaraz por 6-7 (10), 7-5 y 6-3 en 164 minutos de juego gracias, sobre todo, a mantenerse sereno aún cuando el juego no le acompañaba. Eso sí. Será conveniente que en su semifinal ante Casper Ruud o Nuno Borges, consiga que no se repita lo visto ante Taylor Fritz. Porque esta vez bordeó el abismo pero no cayó, pero otra vez podría no tener tanta suerte, aunque la busque como en este partido. El estadounidense es uno de los mejores sacadores del mundo mientras el español es un número 1 mundial, aunque actualmente no ocupe la plaza. En teoría el partido dependería de quién fuera capaz de llevar el partido a su terreno y el primero en hacerlo fue el estadounidense mientras Carlos también lo hizo, pero no era capaz de mantener el partido en ese punto. Fritz empezó ganando nueve puntos seguidos con su servicio -dos juegos en blanco- pero el primero que consiguió Carlos fue preludio de un 'break' que luego prolongó hasta un 5-3 y saque que parecía poner la primera manga en su mano, porque el partido estaba respondiendo a la teoría: con bola en juego y punto más largo Carlos era superior y estaba consiguiendo restar a Taylor y poner en juego la bola. Pero ahí llegó el gran apagón: perdió dos juegos consecutivos en blanco y el primero, con su servicio. Llegó un tie break en el que tuvo 4-2 de ventaja y luego varios puntos de set a favor y en contra, pero en el que cometió errores poco esperables en él. Pero antes esos apagones les costaban partidos. Ahora no tanto. Carlos nunca se desesperó, al menos visiblemente, y esperó su oportunidad con disciplina. Y Carlos Alcaraz consiguió que el partido volviera a su terreno. Se siguió jugando puntos cortos, con poco ritmo, y Taylor ejecutaba solventemente lo que mejor sabe, sacar, y además empezó a jugar de forma más versátil. Carlos cedió su servicio con 3-3 en el segundo set y tuvo luego una bola de break que no pudo aprovechar. Con 3-5, y sacando, salvó puntos de partido con el juego de fantasía que sabe desarrollar, pero sólo le valía para salvar su servicio... ...Y para seguir en el partido. Porque Carlos consiguió recuperar el break para ponerse 5-5, seguir en el partido y llevarse la segunda manga por 7-5 -es decir, ganar tres juegos consecutivos- y ya poder desarrollar un juego más parecido al habitualmente suyo. Podría decirse que cuando Taylor sacaba para ganar con 5-4 le tembló un poco la mano -igual que a Carlos en el primer set-, pero había que estar ahí para aprovecharlo. El tercer set no fue sencillo para Carlos. Se siguió jugando a tirones, sin gran ritmo y Fritz distaba de venirse abajo, pero Carlos había recuperado la seguridad y aunque Carlos rompió pronto, Taylor tuvo también opciones de recuperar el 'break'. Pero la fortaleza mental y la concentración de Carlos ya no volvieron a abandonarle. En otros encuentros de cuartos, Shelton venció a Tommy Paul 6-4, 4-6 y 6-3 y Van Assche a Hijikata 6-4, 6-7, 7-5. Luego jugarán Ruud y Nuno Borges por enfrentarse a Alcaraz.

articles.title: Rafa Jódar llega a las ATP Finals en su primer año como profesional
articles.standfirst: Se convierte en el decimosexto tenista español en jugar el torneo de los maestros
articles.summary: Se convierte en el decimosexto tenista español en jugar el torneo de los maestros
articles.body: La temporada 2026 quedará para siempre ligada a la figura de Rafa Jódar. Tras la victoria de Carlos Alcaraz ante Taylor Fritz en los cuartos de final del Masters 1000 de París, el madrileño, a sus 20 años, se convierte en el primer tenista en la historia en clasificarse a las Nitto ATP Finals en su primer año como profesional. La última edición donde hubo dos españoles en el torneo de los ocho mejores del año fue la de 2015, que juntó a Rafa Nadal y David Ferrer. A Rafa le hacía falta una carambola de casualidades para poder estar del 15 al 22 de este mes en Turín. Con las derrotas del miércoles de De Miñaur y Djokovic, el español necesitaba las eliminaciones de Tommy Paul y Taylor Fritz (el primero antes de la final y el segundo, de la semifinal). Hoy se han cumplido estas dos últimas condiciones de la mano de su compañero de equipo de Copa Davis, Carlos Alcaraz. Se une por tanto a Alexander Zverev, Carlos Alcaraz, Ben Shelton, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils y Frances Tiafoe en el torneo de maestros. En su primera temporada como profesional firma un historial momentáneo de 45 victorias por 18 derrotas. El título conseguido el 5 de abril en Marrakech afirma su condición de campeón ATP. Además de alcanzar hasta en cuatro ocasiones los cuartos de final en torneos de categoría 1000, el último, la final de Shanghái ante Davidovich. Hace siete días se convirtió en el vigesimoprimer español en la historia en entrar al top10 del ranking ATP, tardando tan solo 287 días en hacerlo desde su debut como profesional. Otro récord de precocidad del que se adueñó Jódar, ya que superó al brasileño Gustavo Kuerten, que fijaba la marca en 490 días. Ya son 16 los tenistas españoles que se han clasificado alguna vez en su historia para la Copa de Maestros: Manuel Orantes, Emilio Sánchez Vicario, José Higueras, Sergi Bruguera, Alberto Berasategui, Albert Costa, Carlos Moyá, Alex Corretja, Tommy Robredo, Juan Carlos Ferrero, Rafa Nadal, David Ferrer, Fernando Verdasco, Pablo Carreño, Carlos Alcaraz y hoy, Rafa Jódar, ha añadido su nombre a la laureada lista. Manuel Orantes y Alex Corretja son los únicos que han podido traer el título a España.

articles.title: Paris Masters: Taylor Fritz squanders match points against Carlos Alcaraz as defeat ends hopes of reaching ATP Finals
articles.summary: Season-ending ATP Finals live on Sky Sports from November 15-22, with Spanish youngster Rafael Jodar taking eighth and final spot after Taylor Fritz's defeat to already-qualified Carlos Alcaraz in Paris; Frances Tiafoe's place secured earlier on Friday
articles.body:
Fritz would have reached the end-of-season event in Italy at Rafael Jodar's expense had he beaten Alcaraz to make the last four.

He looked poised to do that after twice finding himself a point from victory in the second set, once on his opponent's serve at 5-3 up and then on his own with the score at 5-4.

However, Alcaraz rallied during a high-quality match to triumph 6-7 (10-12) 7-5 6-3 and ensure he will be joined by compatriot Jodar at the ATP Finals from November 15-22, live on Sky Sports .

Tommy Paul's three-set defeat to fellow American Ben Shelton earlier in the day - US Open finalist Shelton prevailing 6-4 4-6 6-3 - had ended his hopes of reaching the ATP Finals, with countryman Frances Tiafoe's place subsequently secured.

Fritz was looking to become the third US representative in this year's Turin showpiece, after Shelton and Tiafoe, but squandered a golden opportunity to get there and also defeat Alcaraz for just the second time in eight attempts.

The 29-year-old won the first set after a lengthy tie-break and then broke Alcaraz to open up a 4-3 lead in the second set, before saving a break point to make that 5-3.

Alcaraz had already qualified for the ATP Finals - an event he is yet to win in three previous tries - alongside world No 1 Alexander Zverev, Daniil Medvedev, Flavio Cobolli, Arthur Fils, Shelton and Tiafoe.

Home hopes in Turin will rest on Cobolli, with Jannik Sinner - who on Friday announced a split with coach Darren Cahill after five years - ending his campaign early due to a knee problem that has sidelined him since winning Wimbledon in July.

Alcaraz will face Casper Ruud in the semi-finals in Paris after the Norwegian saw off Portugal's Nuno Borges 7-6 (7-5) 6-4, with Shelton meeting home player Luca Van Assche, who overcame Australian qualifier - and Novak Djokovic's conqueror - Rinky Hijikata 6-4 6-7 (4-7) 7-5.

Should we get an Alcaraz-Shelton final in France, it would be a repeat of their five-set epic in the US Open quarter-finals, a match Shelton won in a final-set tie-break at Flushing Meadows.

Alcaraz said after fighting back against Fritz: "I tried not to let myself down in those difficult moments - to stay strong mentally.

"We played incredible tennis, both of us, and I used the energy of the people to give them what they wanted to watch. To entertain them."

articles.title: WTA chair apologises to Jessica Pegula after airing of 'diva' comment
articles.summary: WTA chair Valerie Camillo apologises to Jessica Pegula after her "diva" comment about Mirra Andreeva was live-streamed.
articles.body:
Women's Tennis Association chair Valerie Camillo has apologised to Jessica Pegula and said the live-streaming of private comments to her coach about fellow player Mirra Andreeva was "regrettable and unacceptable".

American Pegula called Andreeva a "diva" in a private conversation with her coach after a practice session for the WTA Tour Finals on Wednesday.

However, the comments were aired on a live stream after the WTA failed to tell players there were microphones on practice courts.

World number five Pegula called the incident "unfortunate" and said the WTA players' council supported players' calls for more privacy.

Camillo said that all audio recording equipment in practice areas had since been removed as "clearly there was a failure in our technical execution and monitoring".

"I want to specifically apologise to Jessica Pegula and [coach] Mark Knowles," she added.

"What happened was regrettable and unacceptable. Jess is one of the WTA's best advocates and biggest stars. She does not deserve this distraction."

WTA takes responsibility after Pegula 'diva' comment live-streamed

Pegula was also heard saying French Open champion Andreeva "needs to be humbled" and her coach Conchita Martinez encourages her behaviour.

A representative for Pegula said she had been in direct contact with those involved and had been "completely unaware" the conversation could be heard by courtside microphones.

None of the players were asked about the incident in the pre-tournament news conference at Indian Wells on Friday, but Pegula did address it in an interview with ESPN.

"I think it's something that we have fought a lot over the last couple years as there's a lot more surveillance and audio and access to the players at tournaments than there has been in the past," she said. , external

"I know for broadcasting that it's great for fans, but I think we've seen a couple incidents now throughout the year, [the] last couple of years really, where it just seems highly unnecessary.

"I think [this will] definitely reignite the topic and, hopefully, we can unfortunately use this incident to keep pushing for more player privacy."

Pegula's compatriot Coco Gauff called for more privacy after she was captured in the players' area smashing a racquet following a defeat by Elina Svitolina in the Australian Open quarter-finals in January.

At the same major, six-time Grand Slam champion Iga Swiatek said players were being watched "like animals in the zoo" by behind-the-scenes cameras.

YouTube streams of Wednesday's practice sessions at Indian Wells have since been removed by the WTA, but the footage had already been shared on social media.

Referring to the incident in California, where the season-ending WTA Finals are being held, Camillo added: "The WTA is sensitive to player privacy and has policies and procedures in place to balance players' needs for safe spaces with opportunities to bring fans closer to the game.

"There was a lack of advanced notice and clear signage to assist players about the recording equipment operating in the area."

articles.title: WTA chair apologises to Jessica Pegula after airing of 'diva' comment about Mirra Andreeva, confirms audio deactivated on practice courts at Indian Wells
articles.summary: Jessica Pegula was heard saying Mirra Andreeva needed to be "humbled" during a practice session ahead of the WTA Finals in California; American hopes incident can help players to "keep pushing for more privacy"; watch tournament from Sunday, live on Sky Sports
articles.body:
US player Pegula describing Russian teenager Andreeva as "a diva" while conversing with coach Mark Knowles during a practice session were heard on a YouTube livestream at Indian Wells, the venue for the WTA Tour season-ending event from November 8-15.

The WTA shouldered the blame for failing to properly inform players about active microphones, with chair Valerie Camillo saying there was "a lack of advanced notice and clear signage" as she confirmed audio will now be switched off for practice sessions.

Camillo added: "I want to specifically apologise to Jessica Pegula and [coach] Mark Knowles. What happened was regrettable and unacceptable.

"Jess is one of the WTA's best advocates and biggest stars. She does not deserve this distraction.

"As a member ​organisation, one of the primary responsibilities of the WTA is to protect ​players whenever possible. The players deserve better and we will continue to work to raise the bar for the WTA."

Pegula: Let's keep pushing for more privacy

Pegula, who was also heard saying French Open champion Andreeva "needs to be humbled" and that her coach, former Wimbledon winner, Conchita Martinez, encouraged her player's behaviour, addressed the incident on ESPN on Friday.

The world No 5 said: "Obviously I had no idea and was not informed that audio was being recorded. But it is what it is.

"I think it's something that we have fought a lot over the last couple years as there's a lot more surveillance, audio and, I guess, access to the players at tournaments than there has been in the past.

"I know for broadcasting that it's great for fans, but I think we've seen a couple incidents now throughout the year, the last couple of years really, where it seems highly unnecessary.

"I think [this will] definitely reignite the topic. Hopefully we can use this incident to keep pushing for more player privacy."

Two-time Grand Slam champion Coco Gauff - in Pegula's group at the WTA Finals, alongside Linda Noskova and world No 1 Elena Rybakina - called for more privacy in January after cameras caught her smashing her racket following defeat to Elina Svitolina at the Australian Open quarter-finals in Melbourne.

articles.title: CPM 22 em Manaus: Show de 30 anos e Digão lotam festival de rock | G1
articles.standfirst: Evento celebrou três décadas de carreira da banda paulista com clássicos do rock nacional e superou as expectativas da produção
articles.summary: O show do CPM 22 em Manaus celebrou 30 anos de carreira com ingressos esgotados e a energia de Digão em um festival que reuniu diferentes gerações de fãs de rock.
articles.body:
CPM 22 e Digão revivem clássicos do rock nacional em festival lotado em Manaus — Foto: Lucas Macedo/g1 AM

O festival Volume Máximo Manaus reuniu uma multidão de fãs de diferentes gerações na última sexta-feira (6), no estacionamento do Amazonas Shopping, na capital amazonense. Com ingressos esgotados e uma atmosfera nostálgica, o evento celebrou clássicos do rock nacional e surpreendeu a organização pelo público.

A programação contou com apresentações da Banda Bates, de Digão, dos Raimundos , acompanhado de Bárbara Wild, e do CPM 22 , que comemorou 30 anos de carreira.

Segundo a produtora Kellen Ketle, o público superou todas as expectativas da organização. "Cara, para mim é surreal. Supriu todas as minhas expectativas, eu não tava esperando esse público. Foi incrível, tá sendo incrível!", celebrou a produtora em meio à euforia da plateia.

CPM 22 celebra conexão com fãs de Manaus

O vocalista do CPM 22, Badauí, destacou a relação da banda com o público manauara, que acompanha o grupo desde as primeiras apresentações na cidade, no início dos anos 2000.

O cantor também ressaltou a renovação dos fãs ao longo das três décadas de carreira e a sintonia com o público durante a turnê comemorativa.

"Desde o primeiro show que a gente fez aqui sempre foi assim. Lá no Tennis Club, lá atrás, em 2001, cara, a gente já, sempre shows lotados e é louco. Porque todas as turnês a gente fez isso, e aí chega nos 30 anos, cara, você vê que teve uma renovação do público, os mais velhos continuam vindo e aí a gente mais nova também", destacou Badauí.

Badauí também comentou sobre as mudanças na indústria musical e a forma como as bandas se comunicam diretamente com os fãs, principalmente pela internet.

"A banda, ela fala diretamente com o seu público, a gente tem os nossos próprios canais de comunicação, então... acho que hoje essa comunicação é direta, não só as bandas brasileiras, as bandas gringas também têm essa comunicação pela internet, e não mais em programas de televisão", disse.

Digão destaca energia do público amazonense

Encerrando a noite, Digão subiu ao palco para tocar clássicos do rock brasileiro. O músico elogiou a energia dos fãs de Manaus e destacou a entrega do público durante as apresentações.

"Manaus é sensacional demais, a galera é muito rock and roll aqui.. O Raimundos quando vem aqui, a galera se entrega mesmo, sabe? Porque tá na veia. Tá na veia, cara, o sangue é quente e rola muito bonito', afirmou Digão.

O artista também falou sobre a experiência de tocar em duo e manter viva a essência do início da carreira.

"Isso é uma coisa muito legal, porque eu mantenho uma chama lá do começo... E hoje a banda, a gente nunca ensaiou junto e tocamos e fomos pra cima. A gente confiou nos anos de rock and roll que a gente tem", afirmou.

articles.title: What Carlos Alcaraz said to Taylor Fritz after eliminating him from ATP Finals contention
articles.summary: Fritz came out on the short end of a highly competitive match where he had two match points
articles.body:
Taylor Fritz had two match points on Carlos Alcaraz on Friday in his Paris Masters quarterfinal. He had taken the first set in a marathon tiebreaker and had all of the momentum leading 5-3 in the second set.

Then, as if a light switch went off, Alcaraz raised his level and got the crowd involved. Fritz needed the win to qualify for the ATP Finals, but 2 hours and 45 minutes later, it was not to be, as Alcaraz won the match in three sets, 6-7, 7-5, 6-3.

The quality of the tennis was high, but many were sad for Fritz who came so close to making the ATP Finals in a year where he battled a knee injury that kept him out of the game for some time. Alcaraz was well aware of what was on the line for Fritz and was ready to talk about it when they met at the net after match point.

The first Alcaraz said to Sinner was that he was sorry. Fritz smiled at him and said he was too good.

Sportsmanship personified between two players who produced a high level of tennis in a grueling match.

This loss will sting for Fritz, but he knows how to manage the emotional highs and lows of the game.

Tommy Paul also knocked out of ATP Finals

Paul lost to Ben Shelton , who finishes the year as the top ranked American for the first time, in Paris ending his bid to make the ATP Finals.

He seemed unbothered about the outcome, either way. His offseason plan was to go fishing . After an eleven month season and a post Wimbledon wedding to longtime girlfriend Paige Lorenze , Paul is ready for some downtime.

Shelton and Frances Tiafoe are the American singles qualifiers for the ATP Finals in Turin. It is Tiafoe's first time playing in the event which features the eight highest ranked players of the 2026 season.

articles.title: Robin Montgomery ends Maaya Rajeshwaran's Chennai Open run
articles.summary: CHENNAI: The week offered wildcard Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi a glimpse of what she could achieve on the big stage.
articles.body: CHENNAI: The week offered wildcard Maaya Rajeshwaran Revathi a glimpse of what she could achieve on the big stage. But her promising run came to an end in the WTA 250 Chennai Open quarterfinals after she went down 3-6, 3-6 to American Robin Montgomery here on Friday.Montgomery, a former junior US Open champion, will face defending champion Janice Tjen, who fought back from a set down to beat Polina Kudermetova 5-7, 6-4, 6-2 in the day’s opening last-eight match.The left-handed Montgomery thrives on pace from her opponents and at times looked uncomfortable when Maaya denied her that luxury. A slow, floating backhand first-serve return from 17-year-old Maaya forced the American to generate her own pace, but she could only find the net.Maaya capitalised and went on to break serve, taking a 3-2 lead. Moreover, world No. 151 Montgomery is prone to unforced errors, having committed 59 in her previous match. Maaya, therefore, needed to keep the ball in play and allow the American’s inconsistency to work against her.The Indian failed to do so, as the 21-year-old reeled off the next four games to close out the set in just 38 minutes.Maaya’s first-serve percentage in the opening set was just 52%, and her second serves were not threatening enough. With Montgomery accustomed to playing at the net, she made good use of the volley when required.In the match between Tjen and Polina, the former took charge after losing the opening. Polina had negated Tjen’s preferred backhand slices in the opening set, with the Uzbek constructing the rallies pretty well.However, from there on, she began throwing away points, committing 45 unforced errors, most of which came in the second and third sets. articles.title: WTA apologises to Pegula for broadcast of ‘diva’ comment about Andreeva
articles.summary: Pegula’s conversation with her coach on a practice court at Indian Wells was broadcast on a WTA YouTube livestream.
articles.body:
Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) chief Valerie Camillo apologised after a courtside microphone captured United States star Jessica Pegula making disparaging comments about rival Mirra Andreeva.

Pegula was plunged into controversy after her conversation with coach Mark Knowles on a practice court at Indian Wells in California was broadcast on a WTA YouTube livestream of the session.

In the exchange, Pegula can be heard describing 19-year-old Russian Andreeva as a “diva”.

World number four Pegula was also heard criticising Andreeva’s coach, former Wimbledon champion Conchita Martinez, for not addressing French Open champion Andreeva’s behaviour.

Speaking before Sunday’s opening matches of the WTA Finals, WTA chairperson Camillo blamed the controversy on “several breakdowns in our execution of the livestream given our own policies and procedures”.

“I want to apologise on behalf of the entire WTA for these occurrences,” Camillo said at a news conference on Friday.

“The WTA is sensitive to player privacy and has policies and procedures in place to balance players’ needs for safe spaces with opportunities to bring fans closer to the game.

“There was a lack of advanced notice and clear signage to assist players about the recording equipment operating in the area,” she added, confirming that all audio recording equipment in practice areas had since been removed.

Camillo said microphones had been installed on practice courts to pick up “ambient sound” – such as the noise of balls being struck – rather than conversations between players and coaches.

“So clearly there was a failure in our technical execution and monitoring,” Camillo said, before directly apologising to Pegula and Knowles.

“I want to specifically apologise to Jessica Pegula and Mark Knowles,” she added.

“What happened was regrettable and unacceptable. Jess is one of the WTA’s best advocates and biggest stars. She does not deserve this distraction.”

The WTA Finals begin on Sunday, with the top eight women’s singles players divided into two round-robin groups of four before advancing to the knockout rounds.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz survives two match points to end Taylor Fritz's ATP Finals hopes
articles.summary: Alcaraz lost an extended first-set tie-break before finishing strong to win 6-7 (10) 7-5 6-3
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz survived two match points against Taylor Fritz to book a spot in the last four of the Paris Masters and end his opponent's hopes of reaching the ATP Finals.

In a lengthy contest that lasted two hours and 43 minutes, the second seed lost an extended first-set tie-break before finishing strong to win 6-7 (10) 7-5 6-3.

Had Fritz taken one of his opportunities in the second set, he would have locked down the eighth and last place in the end-of-year championship. Instead, that spot now goes to Alcaraz's fellow Spaniard Rafael Jodar.

After being outlasted by Fritz in the opener, Alcaraz had to save match points with and against serve in the second, before levelling the scores with three games in a row. He belatedly took control as he closed out the decider in clinical fashion.

Casper Ruud or Nuno Borges await the Spaniard in the semi-finals.

"I tried not to let myself down in the difficult moments in the second set," Alcaraz said.

"I tried to stay strong mentally and save those break points and match points. I used the people and the energy and gave them what they really wanted to watch.

"I am really happy to play for one and a half hours more to entertain them. The feeling I have today is unmatched."

Agregó que el nuevo capitán estará respaldado por otras dos figuras de tenis francés que ya forman parte de la estructura federativa, Gilles Simon y Richard Gasquet. El nombramiento de Monfils se produce en pleno Masters 1.000 de París, donde el jugador tuvo derecho a una ceremonia de despedida, dos meses después de haber disputado en el Abierto de Estados Unidos su último partido. articles.body: El tenis masculino español ha clasificado a tres jugadores para las ATP Finals 2026, que se celebrarán en el Inalpi Arena de Turín del 15 al 22. Allí estarán Carlos Alcaraz y Rafa Jódar, en la competición individual, y Marcel Granollers, en la modalidad del dobles. Todos parten con opciones y con la ambición de estar en las finales del domingo 22. Eso supondría que Alcaraz, Jódar y Granollers no se desplazarían a Bolonia hasta el lunes 23 y no sería hasta el 24 que tendrían el primer entrenamiento real en el Super Tennis Arena de Bolonia para preparar los cuartos de la Copa Davis ante Austria del 26 por la tarde. España, en caso de alcanzar las semifinales, tendrían un día de descanso para enfrentarse al ganador de la serie entre Alemania y Gran Bretaña. David Ferrer, seleccionador nacional, tiene previsto concentrar a sus hombres en la localidad italiana el sábado 21, según ha podido saber MARCA. Sería un día más tarde cuando empezarían las sesiones preparatorias, que podrían ser en familia, con sólo Alejandro Davidovich y Pedro Martínez, en función de los resultados de Turín. Alcaraz y Granollers optaron la pasada campaña por diferentes medios de transporte para completar los 331 kilómetros que separan Turín de Bolonia. Carlitos lo hizo en furgoneta mientras que Marcel viajó en avión desde Barcelona porque fue allí a pasar el fin de semana antes de trasladarse a la ciudad sede de las finales de la Copa Davis.

articles.title: Paris Masters 2026: Carlos Alcaraz’s potential eye-watering prize money revealed as he eyes maiden final after securing €290,960 for reaching semis
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz, after a thrilling semi-final victory, aims for his first Paris Masters title with a staggering €974,370 prize money at stake. Discover his journey and upcoming match details!
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz has reached the semi-finals of the Paris Masters for the first time, but his route to the last four was far from straightforward. The Spaniard saved two match points against Taylor Fritz before completing a three-set comeback, keeping alive his hopes of reaching a maiden final in Paris. A meeting with Casper Ruud now stands between him and a place in Sunday's championship match, with almost €1 million awaiting the eventual winner.Alcaraz has €974,370 in his sights at the Paris MastersCarlos Alcaraz, who is making his sixth appearance at the Paris Masters, has historically found the tournament a challenging venue. The fast indoor hard courts have made it one of his toughest events on the Masters 1000 circuit, and before this year, he had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals. Having finally reached his maiden semi-final, the Spaniard has already secured €290,960. He will face Casper Ruud on Saturday, November 7, with a victory guaranteeing him €532,120 as the runner-up and putting the tournament's €974,370 winner's cheque within reach.According to the ATP Tour's official prize-money breakdown, the 2026 men's singles champion will collect €974,370, while the runner-up receives €532,120. The two players who lose their semi-final matches are each awarded €290,960.The financial difference between the remaining stages is considerable. Beating Ruud would increase Alcaraz's guaranteed earnings by €241,160, while winning the final would take his tournament payout €683,410 above the amount awarded for a semi-final exit. The difference between finishing first and second is €442,250.Champion: €974,370Runner-up: €532,120Semi-finalist: €290,960These awards are determined by a player's final position and are not cumulative. Alcaraz will receive the amount corresponding to his eventual finish rather than adding the payments for each round. The figures also represent tournament prize money before any applicable taxes or expenses.The ATP lists the total prize pool for the event at €6,309,095, covering the tournament as a whole rather than the men's singles competition alone.Alcaraz saves two match points to overturn Taylor FritzThe Spaniard's first Paris Masters semi-final came after one of the most demanding matches of his campaign. Alcaraz defeated Taylor Fritz 6-7(10), 7-5, 6-3 in a quarter-final lasting two hours and 45 minutes, recovering from a position in which the American was twice within a point of victory.Fritz took the opening set in a lengthy tie-break, leaving Alcaraz needing to win the next two sets to stay in the tournament. The American then moved into a 5-3 lead in the second set, putting himself in a strong position to close out the match.Alcaraz first saved a match point on his own serve before holding to reduce the deficit to 5-4. Fritz subsequently had another opportunity to finish the contest while serving for the match, but the Spaniard produced a blistering forehand passing shot to save the second match point and break back.The momentum shifted decisively. Alcaraz won four consecutive games from 3-5 to take the second set 7-5, forcing a deciding set after appearing close to elimination.He carried that momentum into the third, reducing his baseline errors and securing an early break before closing out the set 6-3. The victory also extended his head-to-head advantage over Fritz to 7-1.The match had its share of moments that brought the Paris crowd into the contest. After producing a spectacular point to hold for 4-5 in the second set, Alcaraz encouraged the spectators as he attempted to turn the match around. His recovery from two match points ultimately secured a place in the tournament's final four for the first time.When is Carlos Alcaraz vs Casper Ruud?Alcaraz faces Casper Ruud in Saturday's semi-final, November 7, with the match scheduled to begin not before 9:30 PM IST. The Norwegian reached the last four after defeating Portugal's Nuno Borges 7-6(5), 6-4, continuing a run in which he had progressed through his first four matches in Paris without dropping a set.The upcoming meeting gives Alcaraz an opportunity to reach a first Paris Masters final. He leads Ruud 6-1 in their ATP head-to-head record, although the Norwegian's form during the tournament makes him a significant obstacle.The winner will advance to Sunday's final, scheduled for November 8, not before 7:30 PM IST, against Ben Shelton. Shelton has already secured his place in the championship match and will await the outcome of the Alcaraz-Ruud semi-final.Ranking points provide another incentiveThe prize money is not the only reward at stake for Alcaraz. The Paris Masters also offers a substantial opportunity to collect ranking points before the end of the season, with the ATP awarding 400 points to each losing semi-finalist, 650 to the runner-up and 1,000 to the champion.Alcaraz has already guaranteed himself 400 points by reaching the last four. A victory over Ruud would raise that total to 650, while winning Sunday's final would give him the full 1,000 points available to the champion.For the Spaniard, the immediate objective is to convert his first semi-final appearance in Paris into a maiden final. articles.summary: India's Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale scripted history at the Chennai Open on Saturday, becoming the first all-Indian women's pair to reach a doubles
articles.body: India's Vaishnavi Adkar and Rutuja Bhosale scripted history at the Chennai Open on Saturday, becoming the first all-Indian women's pair to reach a doubles final at the main WTA Tour level. The duo defeated second seeds Weronika Falkowska of Poland and Alana Smith of the USA 6-2, 2-6, 10-8 in a hard-fought semifinal.The Indian pair started strongly but lost their rhythm in the second set.However, they showed great determination in the deciding super tie-break to seal the memorable victory in front of the home crowd.A historic achievement for Indian tennisNo all-Indian women's combination had previously reached a final at the main WTA Tour level. While Shikha Uberoi and her sister Neha reached finals in 2005, Neha represented the USA at the time.Former Indian star Sania Mirza also enjoyed tremendous success in doubles, winning 43 titles, but never achieved those victories with an Indian partner.Ankita Raina and Karman Thandi won a WTA 125 doubles title in 2018, but that tournament belongs to a level below the main Tour.Adkar and Bhosale will now face Swiss pair Naima Karamoko and Simona Waltert in the final. The Swiss duo booked their place after defeating Isabelle Haverlag and Panna Udvardy 6-4, 6-4.How the Indians pulled off the victoryAdkar and Bhosale dominated the opening set, taking a 4-1 lead by making the most of their opponents' mistakes before winning it 6-2.However, Falkowska and Smith bounced back in the second set, taking advantage of missed break opportunities and errors from the Indian pair to win it 6-2 and force a decider.The super tie-break was equally tense, with the opponents opening up a 3-0 lead. articles.summary: El tenista de El Palmar supera a Ruud por séptima vez en su carrera
articles.body: Una semana después de que Ben Shelton anunciara a Juan Carlos Ferrero como su entrenador para 2027, el destino ha querido que el estadounidense se mida este domingo a Carlos Alcaraz en la final del Masters 1000 de París. El morbo está servido si se tiene en cuenta que Alcaraz fue pupilo de Ferrero hasta 2025. Shelton ha perdido tres de los cuatro precedentes con el fenómeno de El Palmar, pero se llevó el último en los cuartos del pasado Abierto de los Estados Unidos. El americano se agarra a su estadística inmaculada en finales de torneos de la categoría. En 2025, venció en Toronto y en 2026, en Montreal. Ben se ganó el billete para la sexta final del curso —las mismas de Carlitos y Jannik Sinner— gracias a remontar a Luca Van Assche. Cerró un marcador favorable de 5-7, 6-3 y 6-4. La grada del Plenitude Arena lloraba la derrota del último compatriota que restaba en el cuadro de la competición individual. “París, te eché de menos”, firmó en la cámara de la realización el miércoles tras su primera victoria en el torneo ante Alex Michelsen. Carlitos, doble campeón de Roland Garros, en 2024 y 2025, se perdió la última edición del Abierto galo por la lesión en su muñeca derecha. El TMS de la capital francesa es otra cosa que no tiene nada que ver con la arcilla de la Philippe Chatrier. En superficie dura bajo techo, sólo David Ferrer fue capaz de inscribir su nombre en el palmarés. Su triunfo llegó en 2012. Pasados 14 años, Alcaraz jugará ante Shelton para secundar al actual capitán español de la Copa Davis. El pupilo de Samuel López le va cogiendo el gustillo al techo. Ya son 44 partidos ganados de 59 disputados, lo que ofrece un porcentaje de efectividad del 74,57 por ciento. Por primera vez en su trayectoria encadena ocho triunfos en ese hábitat. Cabe recordar que hace apenas siete días se coronó en el Open 500 de Viena. Su última víctima ha sido Casper Ruud, por 6-4 y 6-4. Ruud tenía mucha fe en su servicio y por eso eligió sacar tras ganar el sorteo. En el séptimo juego encajó el primer break ante un verdugo que no quería pasar más tiempo del necesario en pista. La jornada del viernes se le había hecho larga con el partido a tres sets ante Taylor Fritz en el que salvó dos pelotas de eliminación. El campeón de siete grandes selló el triunfo con una segunda rotura en el noveno asalto de la continuación. No cedió una sola opción de break a su rival. Así es más fácil. Alcaraz disputará su trigésimo octava final, a sus 23 años y 187 días. De ellas un total de 11 son en Masters 1000. Sólo Rafael Nadal (24) y Novak Djokovic (15) habían disputado más antes de cumplir las 24 primaveras.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz storms to ATP Paris Masters final to set up US Open rematch with Ben Shelton
articles.summary: Season-ending ATP Finals live on Sky Sports from November 15-22, with Spanish youngster Rafael Jodar taking eighth and final spot; Carlos Alcaraz will meet Ben Shelton in the ATP Paris Masters final on Sunday
articles.body:
The Spaniard, who fell in the second round in the same tournament last year, beat his Norwegian opponent 6-4 6-4 to earn a showdown with Ben Shelton on Sunday.

Ruud just about kept Alcaraz at bay in two of his first three service games, but the Spaniard then broke to move 4-3 up and closed out the first set with a 130mph ace.

The second stayed on serve until Alcaraz picked the opportune moment to break to go 5-4 ahead and sealed the win inside just 97 minutes.

This is the sixth final the 23-year-old has reached this calendar year, with him also extending his winning streak to eight consecutive matches.

"This tournament has always been really tough for me. I've struggled every time," Alcaraz said on court.

"I've come into this part of the season much fresher, hungry, ambitious, excited about coming to the tournaments and stepping on the court, playing matches and competing. I'm just really happy that I made the final."

Alcaraz entered the semi-final off the back of a dramatic victory over Taylor Fritz, saving two match points on Friday and apologising to the American at the end for, as Fritz put it at the net, being just "too good".

His drop volley winner against Ruud from the baseline encapsulated his form in the French capital.

The seven-time Grand Slam champion will next face Fritz's compatriot, two months on from their memorable US Open meeting.

World No 4 Shelton beat Alcaraz in the quarter-finals at Flushing Meadows in a gruelling five-set thriller.

Shelton reached the final of the US Open but was ultimately defeated by Alexander Zverev.

In Paris, he secured another final showdown by beating Luca Van Assche 5-7 6-3 6-4 to face Alcaraz once again.

articles.title: Elena Rybakina pulls out of 2026 WTA Finals at Indian Wells due to medical issue and is replaced by Marta Kostyuk
articles.summary: The world No 1 has revealed she is "not physically ready to compete" on Sunday and has been replaced in draw by Marta Kostyuk; You can watch the WTA Finals live on Sky Sports from 8-15 November
articles.body:
The world No 1 was set to face Linda Noskova in the tournament's opening match on Sunday. Her place in Group 1 in the season-ending tournament will now be taken by Marta Kostyuk.

In a statement, the three-time Grand Slam winner said: "I am really sad to inform all my fans and supporters that I unfortunately have to withdraw from the WTA Finals this year.

"I've had an incredible season but my body is just not physically ready to compete. I'm going to spend some time resting and recovering at home and getting myself ready for the 2027 season.

"The WTA Finals is a very special tournament and I wish everyone the best of luck this week. Can't wait to be back in Indian Wells in March!"

Rybakina was going to defend her title that she won going undefeated in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia last year.

The 2025 edition saw her arrive as the last qualifier, but she was the first to earn her spot this year after winning the US Open.

The 27-year-old will still end the season as world No 1 despite the withdrawal, finishing with a 54-14 record and four titles - the Australian Open, Stuttgart, the US Open and Ningbo Open.

Noskova, who became Wimbledon's youngest women's singles champion since Petra Kvitova this summer at the age of 21, will now face world No 10 Kostyuk instead.

articles.title: Paris Masters: Carlos Alcaraz sets up Ben Shelton rematch by beating Casper Ruud to reach final
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz says he is ready for "one of most difficult challenges in tennis" after setting up a rematch against Ben Shelton in the Paris Masters final.
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz says he is ready for "one of the most difficult challenges in tennis" after setting up a rematch against Ben Shelton in the Paris Masters final.

After escaping two match points to pull off a comeback in his quarter-final against Taylor Fritz on Friday, Alcaraz secured his first appearance in the Paris showpiece with an efficient 6-4 6-4 win over Casper Ruud.

The 23-year-old Spaniard's US Open title defence was ended by Shelton in an epic five-set quarter-final which ended at 03:34 local time in their previous meeting in September.

That tournament was seven-time major winner Alcaraz's first following a four-month absence to deal with a wrist injury - and he has been building back towards his scintillating best ever since.

"I'm ready to take on Ben Shelton in the final. It is probably one of the most difficult challenges you can face in tennis right now," said world number three Alcaraz.

"Ben is playing great tennis. Last time, it was a hell of a match. But I'm going to enjoy this moment because I was chasing the final here for a long time. It is going to be a big day for me."

Despite missing a substantial part of the season, only Shelton and Jannik Sinner have matched Alcaraz's six tour-level finals in 2026.

He has lost just one of the 16 matches he has contested since losing to Shelton in New York, and heads into their rematch on an eight-match winning streak after continuing his remarkable injury comeback by triumphing in Vienna last week.

It was a victory over Ruud, in the 2022 US Open final, which allowed Alcaraz to celebrate his maiden major and first world number one ranking.

Continuing his push to re-establish himself at the top of the men's game after long-term injury, Alcaraz proved a class above in his latest encounter with the Norwegian in the French capital on Saturday.

Alcaraz demonstrated all-court superiority as he ended the match having won 86% of points on his first serve, producing 20 winners - including 13 from the forehand - and winning 11 of 13 points at the net in a clinical display.

A single break was enough to settle both sets - he sealed each with an ace for good measure - and denying Ruud any opportunities to reply in the 86-minute win.

Alcaraz, who had never previously gone beyond the quarter-finals in Paris, has now reached the final at seven of the nine prestigious ATP Masters 1000 events.

World number four Shelton awaits after the US Open runner-up completed a three-set comeback victory over Frenchman Luca van Assche.

Shelton, full of confidence late in a 2026 season which has brought a career-best 45 wins, prevailed 5-7 6-3 6-4 to become the first American men's singles finalist at the event since 2017.

"Obviously Carlos is in amazing form. He's a young legend in our sport already and any match he is in is blockbuster," 24-year-old Shelton said.

Shelton may have won their most recent meeting, but Alcaraz won each of their first three and the American has often struggled against the world's best players.

But the US Open win over Alcaraz gave Shelton, who recently appointed Alcaraz's former coach Juan Carlos Ferrero to his team, his first career win over a top-three opponent - and undoubtedly affirmed his belief that he can establish himself at the top of the sport.

articles.title: Elena Rybakina: World number one withdraws from WTA Finals title defence
articles.summary: World number one Elena Rybakina withdraws from the season-ending WTA Finals because of a viral illness.
articles.body:
World number one Elena Rybakina has withdrawn from the WTA Finals because of a viral illness.

Rybakina triumphed at the Australian Open and the US Open in a stellar 2026 as she established herself as the top-ranked women's singles player for the first time.

She was set to begin her bid to emulate American great Serena Williams by becoming the first player since 2014 to win the WTA Finals in back-to-back years on Sunday.

But the 27-year-old Kazakh announced on the eve of the tournament that she would not be able to defend her title in Indian Wells.

"I am really sad to inform all my fans and supporters that I unfortunately have to withdraw from the WTA Finals this year," Rybakina said.

"I've had an incredible season but my body is just not physically ready to compete.

"I'm going to spend some time resting and recovering at home and getting myself ready for the 2027 season."

Rybakina secured her position as the year-end world number one while competing in Tokyo in October.

She had ended Sabalenka's 99-week hold on the top ranking by defeating the Belarusian in the US Open final six weeks earlier.

This season has been the most successful of Rybakina's career, following successes at the Australian Open, US Open, Stuttgart and Ningbo. She also finished runner-up at Indian Wells and Toronto.

Rybakina has won six of her 15 career titles since last October amid a period of sustained success, during which she ended a nearly four-year wait to back-up her maiden slam title at Wimbledon in 2022.

She ends the season having won 54 of her 68 matches, including 17 of 19 in Grand Slam tournaments.

Rybakina's dominance has been founded in tour-leading serve statistics - she landed 438 aces this season, 140 more than second-placed Sabalenka.

But she has also punished opponents with an unrivalled 1,775 winners, and stepped up to the big occasions to record an unmatched 10 wins against fellow top-10 rivals.

articles.title: World No.1 Rybakina withdraws from WTA Finals due to virus
articles.summary: World number one Elena Rybakina withdrew from the WTA Finals at Indian Wells on Saturday due to a viral illness.A WTA spokesman later confirmed that the offi...
articles.body:
World number one Elena Rybakina withdrew from the WTA Finals at Indian Wells on Saturday due to a viral illness.

Defending champion Rybakina said in a statement that she was "not physically ready to compete" in the traditional season-ender, which starts Sunday, and would focus on resting and recovering for her 2027 campaign.

"I am really sad to inform all my fans and supporters that I unfortunately have to withdraw from the WTA Finals this year," Rybakina said in a statement.

"I've had an incredible season but my body is just not physically ready to compete.

"I'm going to spend some time resting and recovering at home and getting myself ready for the 2027 season."

A WTA spokesman later confirmed that the official reason for Rybakina's withdrawal "is a viral illness."

Ukraine's Marta Kostyuk will take Rybakina's place in Group One at the tournament.

Rybakina rose to the top of the world rankings for the first time in September with a victory at the US Open in New York, where she defeated Aryna Sabalenka in the final.

But last month, Rybakina withdrew from the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo with a neck injury, a day after she secured the year-end world number one ranking with a win in her opening match.

The achievement capped a year in which Rybakina also won the Australian Open in January.

She now has three Grand Slam titles, her first coming at Wimbledon in 2022.

Rybakina went undefeated at the 2025 edition of the WTA Finals in Riyadh, Saudi Arabia as the last qualifier.

This year's WTA Finals were originally scheduled to be held in Saudi Arabia, but in July were moved to Indian Wells, California.

The decision was taken following US military strikes on Iran in February and the subsequent war in the region.

Several more sports events in Saudi Arabia have been cancelled or postponed in recent weeks following attacks on the country.

"The WTA Finals is a very special tournament and I wish everyone the best of luck this week. Can't wait to be back in Indian Wells in March," said Rybakina in a statement released by the WTA.

articles.title: Tennis world number one Rybakina withdraws from WTA Finals due to virus
articles.summary: Rybakina pulled out on the eve of the Indian Wells tournament, with Ukraine’s Marta Kostyuk replacing the top seed.
articles.body:
Defending champion Elena Rybakina has pulled out of the Women’s Tennis Association (WTA) Finals, saying she was not physically ready to compete, allowing Ukraine’s Marta Kostyuk to take her place in the eight-player field at Indian Wells.

Organisers on Saturday cited a viral illness as the official reason for the world number one’s “disappointing” withdrawal, but said the world number one needs time to recover from the physical toll of a demanding year.

Tournament director Garbine Muguruza, a former world number one and two-time Grand Slam champion, said she had spoken with Rybakina and that the Kazakh had been unable to recover in time after struggling with physical problems late in the season.

“We love Elena, and we know that she was feeling so-so in Tokyo as well,” Muguruza told the Reuters news agency. “I spoke to her today, and she really couldn’t recover on time.

“What we want is for her to feel good, to go rest, to recover. We don’t want her to feel like she has to play — only if she’s ready to.”

Rybakina, who won two Grand Slam titles this year, also withdrew from ⁠the quarterfinals of the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo last month because of a neck injury.

‘Amazing field’ despite Rybakina absence

Rybakina’s absence deprives the event of some star power, but Muguruza said the round-robin format and depth of the field would ensure a high-quality tournament.

“We have the best players,” said Muguruza, who triumphed at the WTA Finals in Guadalajara in 2021.

“I know our world number one is not going to be able to play, but we have an amazing field, the very best,” she added.

“Every match could be a Grand Slam final. You really need to be ready. You cannot give one inch.”

Kostyuk, who is making her WTA Finals debut after a breakthrough season that included the Madrid title and a rise into the top 10, was already in Indian Wells as an alternate and practising when Rybakina withdrew.

Muguruza said the Ukrainian, known for her signature post-match backflip celebrations, had earned her opportunity.

“Marta is great. She’s had a breakthrough year,” Muguruza said. “With this year, we have many first-time players in the Finals, and that’s very exciting. It’s very hard to qualify.”

Kostyuk has been outspoken about Russia’s invasion of Ukraine and does not shake hands with Russian or Belarusian opponents. Muguruza said the tournament would support players in making their own decisions.

“They’re free to do whatever they feel,” she said. “We are open and supporting them.”

Rybakina’s withdrawal could create an opening for world number two Aryna Sabalenka to make inroads in the rankings.

Sabalenka, who won the Indian Wells title earlier this year, has the chance to reduce the gap at the top of the rankings, according to Muguruza, who highlighted Russian teenager Mirra Andreeva as a player comfortable in the California desert.

“Of course, Aryna might be thinking that this can be a good opportunity,” she said.

The WTA moved the finals to Indian Wells from Riyadh, Saudi Arabia, with Muguruza saying player safety had been the decisive consideration amid conflict in the Middle East region.

“It clearly felt no longer safe to be in a region where there is conflict,” she said. “Taking care of the players and looking ahead to what could be safe, comfortable and secure, relocating felt the best decision.”

Muguruza said players had responded positively to the switch to Indian Wells, where she competed regularly during her career.

“When we knew that Indian Wells could be the next venue, it was just a joy,” she said, adding that ticket sales have been strong. “The whole thing is just perfect.”

articles.title: Alcaraz - Shelton: resumen, resultado y estadísticas de la final del Masters 1000 de París
articles.summary: Lo dejamos por aquí hoy. Disponible la crónica del partido en MARCA. Seguro que seguiremos teniendo grandes noticias de Carlos Alcaraz en el futuro. L
articles.body:
Última hora del Alcaraz - Shelton, en directo

Buenas tardes, bienvenidos a la final del Masters 1000 de París. Hoy tendremos en la pista central de La Défense Arena a Carlos Alcaraz, que se las verá ante Ben Shelton por la posibilidad de levantar su quinto título del año. El partido se disputará alrededor de la 15:00 horas (horario local).

Una semana después de que el americano anunciara su enlace profesional junto a Juan Carlos Ferrero para 2027, los dos tenistas se ven las caras por primera vez en una final de un gran torneo. El TMS galo es otro de los torneos que se le suele resistir al tenis español. David Ferrer fue el último integrante de la 'Armada' en levantar el certamen bajo techo, cuando se impuso en 2012. Hoy, Alcaraz puede romper la mala racha. El fenómeno de El Palmar ha mejorado en esta superficie. Firma 44 victorias en 59 partidos disputados. Y viene con una estela de ocho victorias consecutivas bajo estas condiciones. La última, la séptima victoria ante Casper Ruud en semifinales.

El murciano se ha llevado tres de los cuatro precedentes ante Ben Shelton. Aunque el americano se apuntó el último en los cuartos del pasado US Open. Un duelo que estiró hasta las cuatro horas y 31 minutos, terminando a las 3:33 de la madrugada neoyorquina. El morbo está servido si se tiene en cuenta que Juan Carlos Ferrero fue el entrenador de Alcaraz hasta inicios de 2025.

articles.title: Tearful Alex Eala loses Hong Kong Open final to Claire Liu in straight sets
articles.summary: Philippine tennis star Eala stunned after 6-3, 6-0 loss to the 102nd-ranked American in Hong Kong.
articles.body:
Tennis trailblazer Alex Eala from the Philippines burst into tears as she reflected on a “life-changing” season after falling agonisingly short of a second WTA Tour title in Hong Kong.

The second seed was stunned 6-3, 6-0 by Claire Liu in the final of the Hong Kong Open as the American, ranked 102nd, won her first tour title on Sunday.

Eala is at a career-high 17 in the world after a breakout year in which the 21-year-old clinched her maiden title, in Washington, DC, in August.

That victory made her the first player from the Philippines to win a tournament on the WTA Tour.

Eala, set to rise to world number 15 next week, started the year ranked 50th.

“This season has changed my life; it’s changed my life for the better,” Eala, who finished the final with heavy strapping on her right leg, told the crowd afterwards.

Becoming emotional as she addressed her team in the stands, she said: “I’m incredibly proud of the work we’ve put in this year.

“We’re the only ones that truly know what it took to arrive to this point in our journey.

articles.standfirst: El murciano, doble campeón de Roland Garros, gana bajo la cubierta de La Défense
articles.summary: El murciano, doble campeón de Roland Garros, gana bajo la cubierta de La Défense
articles.body: Carlos Alcaraz, verdugo de Ben Shelton, por 7-6(5) y 7-5, ya puede tachar de la lista de objetivos el torneo de París, uno de los tres Masters 1000 que le faltaban, junto a Canadá y Shanghái. David Ferrer, vencedor en la edición de 2012, ya tiene quien le acompañe en el palmarés. A sus 23 años y 188 días, sólo le restan las ATP Finals y la Copa Davis entre los grandes títulos. Y estos dos eventos vienen a continuación en el calendario del fenómeno de El Palmar. La multinacional Nike ya puede ir preparando una camiseta conmemorativa como la que ha lucido estos días en el multiusos de La Défense, añadiendo la cita de maestros y la máxima competición por países. Alcaraz empezó la gira europea en superficie dura bajo techo superando por los pelos el 70 por ciento de éxito en sus apariciones en ese hábitat. Después de sus dos coronas en Viena y en París, ha elevado ese porcentaje de efectividad al 75 por ciento. Su balance es de 45 partidos ganados a cubierto por 15 perdidos. Para encontrar el último traspié hay que remontarse a la final de las ATP Finals 2025 contra Jannik Sinner. El italiano no es rival esta vez para el español al permanecer lesionado de la rodilla desde Wimbledon. Carlitos se supera a sí mismo y ha establecido este domingo, en la central del Plenitude Arena, un tope personal. Y es que nunca antes se había llevado dos trofeos en el margen de siete días. Es el intervalo de tiempo que pasó desde que venció a Alex de Miñaur en Viena y derrotó a Shelton en el Masters 1000 de la capital gala. Los 28 entorchados anteriores siempre habían llegado con más separación entre ellos. El pupilo de Samuel López ya echa el aliento a Manolo Orantes (34), entre los españoles más laureados de la Era Open. Por delante está Rafael Nadal (92). Alcaraz no había escondido las ganas que le tenía a Shelton, su verdugo en los cuartos del último US Open. Tenía que cambiar detalles en los momentos importantes y tenía bien aprendida la lección. El estadounidense, invicto en finales de torneos TMS —había ganado en Toronto 2025 y Montreal 2026— ya sabe lo que es hincar la rodilla. El campeón de siete grandes rompe cualquier techo con su arsenal de golpes. No tiene una dependencia absoluta en el servicio, algo que sí le pasa a Ben y a la mayoría de sus adversarios. Shelton ganó el sorteo y eligió servir. Los dos primeros puntos de la final fueron un ace y un saquetazo. A la que llegó el primer intercambio, Carlitos conectó un pasante. Era la carta de presentación de ambos. Ben fue el primero en inquietar a su oponente, con cuatro opciones de break en el cuarto juego. Tres de ellas fueron con un 0-40. La vara de medir en el juego del español es la derecha y le iba a mil. Los dos agujeros del americano son claros y sabidos: el revés y las subidas a la red. "Anímate mucho, tú sigue así, poco a poco", le transmitía Samu a su pupilo desde la primera fila. El número cuatro mundial no daba opción con el servicio y eso podía desesperar a cualquiera. Alcaraz dispuso después de una doble oportunidad de rotura en el séptimo asalto. Su rival volvió a la carga, con un 4-3 y 15-40. El campeón supo manejar el momento de máxima presión y su víctima no. La tensión se palpaba en el ambiente. "Vamos suelto", decía Samu. Con un raquetazo a 218 kilómetros por hora, Shelton se aseguró la muerte súbita del primer set. La perdió después cuando dominaba por 4-3 en el parcial. Fue el principio del fin para él. Carlitos fue capaz de darle la vuelta a un 2-4 adverso en la continuación, con algunos pasantes que echaban humo. La cita de maestros y la lucha por la Ensaladera de plata se jugarán en la misma pista GreenSet y en la misma cubierta que han visto ganar a Carlitos en Viena y París. El único cambio serán las pelotas: de las Dunlop a las Yonex. Este jueves conocerá sus rivales en el grupo de Turín y el domingo, otros siete días después, empieza el último sprint del curso. Carlitos y Ben podrían volver a verse las caras en el Masters. De momento, cuatro victorias a una para el primero en el cara a cara.

articles.title: Spain's Alcaraz wins Paris Masters for first time
articles.summary: Carlos Alcaraz gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton on Sunday as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris M...
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz gained a measure of revenge on Ben Shelton on Sunday as the seven-time Grand Slam champion beat the American 7-6 (7/5), 7-5 to win the Paris Masters for the first time.

In defeating the man that ended his US Open title defence earlier this season, the 23-year-old Spaniard claimed the ninth 1000-level title of his career.

Unlike their five-set quarter-final epic in New York two months ago, the clash in Paris lasted just under two hours.

Ahead of the ATP Finals, which run November 15-22 in Turin, world number three Alcaraz now holds five tour-level titles this year -- only the injured Jannik Sinner has more with six.

In Italy, he will be seeking a first coronation at the season-ender.

After winning two French Opens and now the Paris Masters, Alcaraz is undefeated in title matches in the city.

But not for the first time in the French capital, Alcaraz won the title by saving match points en route -- this time against Taylor Fritz in the quarter-finals in scenes reminiscent of his iconic Roland Garros final win against Italian Sinner last year.

For world number four Shelton, it was a first defeat in a Masters final after winning his two previous appearances in showpiece matches at that level-- both coming in the last two editions of the Canadian Open.

Serving at 1-2 in the first set, Alcaraz flirted with danger as he offered up four break points, but dug in to secure the hold when Shelton misfired at the end of a seven-minute long game.

Shelton then found himself two break points down in the seventh game but responded with a perfect drop volley and blistering passing shot to bring up deuce, before holding and keeping his nose in front.

Although both players threatened on the other's serve and drew repeated gasps from the crowd with some audacious shot-making, the opener nonetheless required a tie-break to separate them.

A Shelton error at 4-4 followed by a leaping backhand smash by Alcaraz brought up two set points.

The first came and went when Alcaraz thundered the ball into the top of the net cord and the expectant arena froze in time as it rose and fell in seeming slow motion, only to land on the Spaniard's side of the court.

Alcaraz was not to be denied a second time, however, as Shelton overcooked a forehand on the next point to cede the opener.

At 2-2 in the second set, Shelton let out a bellow of frustration after missing a groundstroke at 15-30 on Alcaraz's serve, but the American could smile at the end of the game as a double fault and missed forehand produced the first break of the match.

Alcaraz had said after booking his spot in the final that his reflexes would need to be "ten out of ten" when facing Shelton's serve and they were just that three games later as he levelled the set at four-all.

A deft exchange of angled drop shots ended by an Alcaraz winner down the line brought the Spaniard's finger to his ear and the crowd again to their feet as Shelton suddenly found himself serving to keep the final alive.

He did so at the first time of asking but when required to serve again to force a breaker, Shelton cracked as Alcaraz again pounced to seal the title with a flicked backhand winner.

articles.body:
Alcaraz edged a thrilling opening set, roaring towards the Paris crowd after clinching the tie-break. Neither player could find a breakthrough in a set lasting 65 minutes, with Shelton unable to convert any of his six break-point opportunities.

The second set looked to be taking a similar course of action until Shelton shocked Alcaraz with a break to love at 3-2, firing two aces past his opponent in the game, but Alcaraz bounced back with a break at the earliest opportunity to bring the scores back to level at 4-4.

The world No 3 seized the momentum, firing up the crowd before producing a stunning winner off a Shelton drop shot to secure the crucial break, take the second set 7-5 and claim the championship.

Alcaraz's maiden Paris title marks his ninth consecutive match win and fifth tournament victory from six finals in 2026. It also exacts revenge on Shelton, who beat him in a gruelling 4hr 28min US Open quarter-final in September.

articles.title: Carlos Alcaraz defeats Ben Shelton in thrilling final for first Paris Masters title
articles.summary: The Spaniard triumphed 7-6(5) 7-5 in a tight encounter to win the Paris title for the first time in his career
articles.body:
Carlos Alcaraz 's excellent comeback continued as he defeated Ben Shelton 7-6(5) 7-5 to claim the Paris Masters title for the first time.

World No 3 Alcaraz missed nearly five months of the 2026 season with a wrist injury and his initial comeback came to an end at Shelton's hands, with the American triumphing in a epic five-setter in the US Open quarter-finals.

Since then Alcaraz has lifted ATP 500 titles in Tokyo and Vienna, the latter just last week.

Despite not playing at his fluid best he scraped through in Paris - saving two match points against Taylor Fritz in the quarter-finals - and he continued his late-season surge with victory in an entertaining encounter between two of the tour's flair players and his first meeting with Shelton since New York.

Shelton made an assured start on serve and it was Alcaraz who came under pressure first, falling 0-40 down as the American led 2-1. But the Spaniard saved four break points to hold in a near eight-minute game, with a combination of deft volleys and aggression from the back of the court.

Both players struggled to take their chances as Shelton saved two break points - one with a sublime angled volley - to keep things on serve for a 4-3 lead, then spurned another two chances to break before Alcaraz held for 4-4 with a punishing, unreturned first serve.

Inevitably the first set went to a tiebreak, a contest of frequent momentum swings as eight of the 12 points went against serve. Shelton battled back from 1-3 down with an explosive smash while back-pedalling to the baseline, but could not press his advantage home.

Alcaraz set up two set points with a fierce backhand volley, spurning the first thanks to an unhelpful net cord which just dipped back onto his side, but let out a roar of relief as Shelton blasted a forehand wide to concede the first set 7-6(5) in just over an hour.

US Open runner-up Shelton won his previous three matches in Paris in three sets and would be forced to attempt another escape act, starting from 0-30 down in his first service game of the second set.

Four big first serves helped him out of trouble and he was rewarded for his patience as he finally broke Alcaraz's serve for a 3-2 lead, the first break of the match, with a fierce angled return that Alcaraz could only send long.

A superb overhead smash from the American in the next game led to the first sign of genuine frustration for Alcaraz, who mimed throwing his racquet to the ground, as Shelton held to love.

The seven-time major winner was not at his best but took advantage of a dip in concentration by Shelton to break back to 15 in his next service game, levelling things for 4-4.

A superb point in the next game encapsulated the match: Shelton didn't do a lot wrong in a finely-balanced rally until he sent a volley straight back at the Spaniard, with Alcaraz capitalising on acres of open space to plant the winner behind him, geeing up the appreciative crowd on his way to a hold to 15.

A much more relaxed Alcaraz smiled and danced along to Abba's 'Gimme! Gimme! Gimme!' at the next changeover and kept the pressure on as the pair exchanged holds.

With Shelton serving to stay in the match, Alcaraz retrieved a brilliant lob from the back of the court and lashed a stunning forehand around the outside of the post for 15-30.

Shelton hit long to gift the Spaniard two championship points; he sprayed the first one wide but sealed the second with another superb point, covering every inch of the court before another forehand winner. He jumped for joy as he sealed his ninth Masters 1000 title and first in Paris before running to celebrate with his team and parents.

Shelton may have the chance for revenge as early as next week, as the pair have both qualified for the season-ending ATP Finals, which begin on 15 November in Turin.
